title: Preregistration: Block V Reflective Self-Modelling - Theory of Everything Research Programme
author: Kenneth Craggs

hypotheses.wording: Self-monitoring improves behaviour primarily when self-related estimates can alter subsequent computation or action.

decision_rule.retain_if: Across both held-out self-relevant task families, mean S2-minus-S1 accuracy is >=0.12 and at least 18/20 seeds favour S2; on matched self-irrelevant controls the absolute S2-minus-S1 mean accuracy difference is <=0.05.
decision_rule.restrict_if: The active-monitor benefit is reliable in only one registered task family or the matched irrelevant-task specificity criterion fails.
decision_rule.reduce_if: S1 passive monitoring matches S2 across both decisive self-relevant families.
decision_rule.reject_if: Allowing the self-monitor to influence control produces no reproducible selective benefit.

hypotheses.wording: Active self-monitoring improves recovery after unannounced internal impairment.

decision_rule.retain_if: For both held-out task families, post-impairment S2 accuracy exceeds S1 by >=0.15, the median S2 detection latency is <=3 episodes, mean self-estimated reliability falls by >=0.10 after impairment, and at least 18/20 seeds favour S2.
decision_rule.restrict_if: Recovery benefit or reliable detection is present in only one registered family.
decision_rule.reduce_if: Recovery is matched by S1 or occurs without a corresponding decrease in the nominated self-estimate.
decision_rule.reject_if: Active self-monitoring does not improve post-impairment recovery.

hypotheses.wording: Manipulating self-related estimates causes predictable changes in reflective control, and restoring accurate estimates rescues behaviour.

decision_rule.retain_if: In both registered task families, induced overconfidence reduces the adaptive checking/compute response and lowers mean accuracy by >=0.15 relative to the accurate condition; restoration recovers >=0.15 mean accuracy and returns the action-allocation rate to within 0.05 of the accurate condition; at least 18/20 seeds show the predicted failure-rescue direction.
decision_rule.restrict_if: The manipulation-rescue sequence is reliable in only one task family.
decision_rule.reduce_if: Behaviour recovers comparably without restoring the nominated self-estimate.
decision_rule.reject_if: Direct self-estimate misinformation produces no selective predicted behavioural effect.

hypotheses.wording: Episode-specific self-monitoring provides more useful control than shuffled or distribution-matched monitoring signals.

decision_rule.retain_if: Under the preregistered unannounced-impairment recovery assay, S2 exceeds S3 post-impairment accuracy by >=0.15 in the decision family and >=0.10 in the verification family, with at least 18/20 seeds favouring S2 in each family; the S3 construction must preserve the exact marginal monitor-value multiset.
decision_rule.restrict_if: State-specific correspondence matters in only one family.
decision_rule.reduce_if: Distribution-matched S3 reproduces S2 recovery across both families.
decision_rule.reject_if: Breaking episode-specific monitor correspondence has no reproducible effect.

hypotheses.wording: The agent tracks at least some internally generated capability changes rather than only environmental uncertainty.

decision_rule.retain_if: With external difficulty held fixed, self-monitor mean absolute error to true success probability is >=0.05 lower than world-only uncertainty, mean self-estimate decreases by >=0.10 under internal impairment, world-only estimate changes by <=0.02, and at least 18/20 seeds show the self-monitor MAE advantage.
decision_rule.restrict_if: Self-specific tracking appears only for one impairment type or capability boundary.
decision_rule.reduce_if: World-only uncertainty reproduces the decisive calibration and impairment-tracking effects.
decision_rule.reject_if: The nominated self-estimate does not track internally generated capability change.

hypotheses.wording: Reflective self-modelling provides functions not fully reproduced by simpler task-specific error detection or externally supplied confidence.

decision_rule.retain_if: S2 exceeds every preregistered bypass (S4, H_ERROR and H_EXTERNAL) by >=0.10 mean accuracy or utility on both decisive held-out families and at least 18/20 seeds favour S2 over every bypass.
decision_rule.restrict_if: S2 exceeds the task-specific and world-only bypasses but an information-equivalent external-confidence bypass remains within 0.05 on one decisive family.
decision_rule.reduce_if: H_EXTERNAL remains within 0.05 of S2 on both decisive families and reproduces the misinformation-independent downstream control benefit, showing that access to calibrated self-relevant information rather than endogenous generation is sufficient for the registered function.
decision_rule.reject_if: A simpler non-self or task-specific bypass reproduces the full decisive cross-family profile without access to calibrated self-relevant information.

development_use: Development-only results informed task/control hardening and prospective thresholds but are excluded from confirmatory evidence.
